title: Topwater command
description: One built-in command. tools/spec-gen/gen.py turns these files into tables for the three ports; see spec/README.md.

name.description: The command name the agent types. The file is spec/commands/<name>.json, with . : [ spelled dot colon bracket.

summary.description: One line, no final period: what `help` lists, and the second line of the default --help.

ports.description: The ports that have this command. Absent: all three. Anything else is a known gap, listed in spec/README.md.

shellBuiltin.description: Part of bash itself: `type` says 'shell builtin' and errors are prefixed 'bash: '.

programFile.description: Whether /usr/bin/<name> exists (false for builtins a real system has no program for).

standardOptions.description: Whether a lone --help / --version is answered with help / version (false: the command sees them as arguments).

help.description: The --help text, one string per line (a final newline is added). Default: 'Usage: <name> [OPTION]... [ARG]...' then '<summary>.'. `help <name>` prints it only when given here.

reportsAs.description: The program name in usage errors when it differs from name (egrep reports as grep).

usageExitCode.description: Exit status after a bad option or a missing operand.

tryHelp.description: The lines after a usage error. Default: "Try '<name> --help' for more information.".

parser.description: args: the shared getopt-style parser reads `options` (generated into each port). custom: the command parses its own arguments; `options` is documentation.

exitCodes.description: What each exit status means, when more than success/failure.

messages.description: Diagnostic templates, keyed by a camelCase id the code uses. Placeholders: {name}, {name:shell}, {name:shell-always}, {name:locale}; see spec/README.md. Usually the text after the '<name>: ' prefix the port adds; a message of another shape (a leading newline, several lines, another program's prefix) is stored whole. A key missing here falls back to shell.json's defaults.messages.

subcommands.description: For a command with subcommands (git): one entry per subcommand name. The command uses parser 'custom' and dispatches itself; each subcommand parses with its own generated option table. See spec/README.md.

summary.description: One line, no final period: what the command's help lists for this subcommand.

usage.description: Usage lines without the 'usage: ' prefix (added to the first line, the others indented to match).

help.description: The full help text, one string per line. Default (generated): the usage lines, a blank line, the summary with a period, then one line per option.

ports.description: The ports that have it. Absent: all that have the command.

unsupported.description: Recognised but not available in this machine: the command prints its own message for it and fails.

options.description: Same shape as a command's options; their generated table is what the subcommand parses with.

messages.description: Diagnostic templates for this subcommand; a key missing here falls back to the command's messages, then shell.json's defaults.messages.

long.description: Names after '--' that mean the same option.

key.description: The letter the code looks the option up by, when it is not `short` (long-only options use a control character).

arg.description: Present when the option takes a value: its name in help text (NUM, FILE...).

description.description: What Topwater does with it, in our own words (never a real program's help text).

ports.description: The ports that accept it. Absent: all that have the command.

custom.description: The command reads this option itself before the shared parser, so it stays out of the generated table.

ignored.description: Accepted but without effect: true in every port that accepts it, or the list of ports where it does nothing.
